cards.text: Welcome in, friend. This book opens with the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem. Right out of the gate he says it TWICE, in case somebody in the back missed it: "Futility of futilities," says the Teacher, "futility of futilities!"

cards.question: Right away, the Teacher says only some things are futile.

cards.text: EVERYTHING, friend, and he doesn't even say good morning first. Then he asks a question about all the labor a man toils at under the sun.

cards.question: The Teacher looks at all the labor a person toils at under the sun. What does he ask about it?

answers.text: What a man gains from it
How long a man must keep at it
Who a man is working for

cards.text: Then the Teacher zooms WAY out and looks at people across time. Generations come, and generations go.

cards.question: Generations come and generations go, but the Teacher says the earth ___ forever.

cards.text: Then the Teacher looks up at the sun. It rises, and it sets.

cards.question: After the sun sets, what does the Teacher say it does?

answers.text: Hurries back to where it rises

cards.text: Then the Teacher turns to the wind, blowing southward and then turning northward. That wind has my sense of direction, friend.

cards.question: The Teacher watches the wind blow southward, then turn northward. What does he say it keeps doing?

cards.text: Then the Teacher looks at the rivers. All of them flow into the sea.

cards.question: All the rivers flow into the sea, yet the Teacher says the sea is never full.
All the rivers flow into the sea. Where does the Teacher say the streams flow again?

answers.text: Back to the place they came from

cards.text: Then the Teacher says all things are wearisome, more than one can describe. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer counting falling dust, and wearisome doesn't even BEGIN to cover it.

cards.question: The Teacher says all things are wearisome. What does he say about the eye and the ear?

answers.text: They lose their strength with age
They catch only what is near

cards.text: Then the Teacher looks at what has been and what has been done, and says it will all be done again. Stamp, bake, box, repeat: that's my whole week, and I LOVE it.

cards.question: The Teacher says there is nothing ___ under the sun.

cards.text: The Teacher asks: is there ever a case where someone can say, "Look, this is new"? He says it already existed in the ages before us, and there is no remembrance of those who came before.

cards.question: The Teacher also talks about people yet to come. He says they will be remembered by those who follow after them.
